subject: ent
title: Sinonasal tumours and granulomatous conditions

steps.tx: Benign sinonasal tumours usually cause one sided nasal blockage with discharge and repeated nosebleeds. **Inverted papilloma** typically arises from the lateral nasal wall or maxillary sinus in middle aged men and can erode nearby bone. About 5 to 10 percent develop associated **squamous carcinoma**, so complete endoscopic removal with drilling of the bony origin is essential. Long follow up is needed because recurrence is common. **Osteomas** of the frontal sinus and **juvenile angiofibroma** in teenage boys complete the classic benign group.
steps.say: A one sided nasal mass in a middle aged man is usually an inverted papilloma. It grows inward from the side wall of the nose and can destroy surrounding bone. A small fraction of cases develops coexisting squamous cancer, so surgeons remove the whole lesion. They also remove the bony attachment and keep the patient under review for several years.

steps.tx: **Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma** is a highly vascular benign tumour that grows near the **sphenopalatine foramen** in teenage boys, usually under androgen influence. It causes progressive nasal blockage with recurrent heavy nosebleeds. Imaging shows a vascular blush with bone erosion on CT, flow voids on MRI and feeding vessels from the internal maxillary artery on angiography. Outpatient biopsy is forbidden because of bleeding risk, so modern care uses **preoperative embolisation** followed by endoscopic resection.
steps.say: A teenage boy with a blocked nose and repeated heavy bleeds probably has an angiofibroma. This vascular tumour arises near the back of the nasal cavity and erodes surrounding bone. Scans reveal a rich blood supply with enlarged feeding vessels from the maxillary artery. Doctors must never take a clinic biopsy because the bleeding can become uncontrollable. They block the feeding vessels first and then remove the tumour through the endoscope.

steps.tx: Sinonasal **malignancies** usually present late with one sided nosebleeds, blockage, facial pain and loss of smell. **Squamous carcinoma** is the commonest type, while ethmoid **adenocarcinoma** affects hardwood dust workers and olfactory neuroblastoma arises from the smell receptive area. Nickel exposure, leather work and viral associations differ across tumour types. Advanced disease invades the orbit causing bulging eyes or double vision, loosens teeth or produces a palatal lump. MRI separates tumour from trapped secretions, CT maps bone destruction, and endoscopic biopsy follows imaging once vascular lesions are excluded.
steps.say: Sinonasal cancers declare themselves late with bleeding on one side and a blocked nose. Facial pain, loosening teeth and loss of smell point toward a malignant growth. Workers exposed to wood dust carry a higher risk of ethmoid adenocarcinoma. Scans map the tumour and separate it from blocked mucus before surgeons take a biopsy. Orbital swelling or double vision means the cancer has already spread beyond the sinuses.

steps.tx: The coronal scan shows a left sided sinonasal **tumour mass** eating through the **lamina papyracea** into the orbit, pushing the globe into **proptosis**. This matches the malignancy step where late disease invades the eye, loosens teeth, or forms a palatal lump. In the exam, link proptosis with double vision, MRI separation of tumour from trapped secretions, and biopsy only after vascular lesions are excluded.
steps.say: This coronal scan presents a left sided nasal tumour that has eaten through the paper thin wall into the eye socket. The globe bulges forward into a proptosis that requires urgent specialist review. Such invasion produces double vision and marks advanced disease. Scans separate tumour from trapped secretions above it, and biopsy follows only after vascular tumours are excluded.

steps.tx: Midline destructive disease of the nose includes **granulomatosis with polyangiitis**, which causes crusting, septal perforation and saddle nose deformity. Cocaine induced midline injury mimics vasculitis and can distort antibody tests, so drug history matters. Extranodal **NK T cell lymphoma** of nasal type is an EBV driven necrotic midline tumour that needs repeated edge biopsies with haematology input. Sarcoidosis and tuberculosis can mimic the same picture. Regional infections such as **rhinoscleroma** and rhinosporidiosis also form granulomatous masses in endemic areas.
steps.say: A crusted and collapsing midline nose suggests vasculitis, cocaine injury, lymphoma or chronic infection. Blood tests for antineutrophil antibodies support the diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Cocaine related lesions mimic vasculitis closely, so doctors always ask about drug use. Nasal type NK T cell lymphoma destroys midline tissue and links strongly to Epstein Barr virus. Surgeons biopsy the living edge repeatedly because dead centre tissue rarely gives the answer.
